newsitem.title: UK: BA shares squeezed to record high.
newsitem.headline: BA shares squeezed to record high.

text.p: British Airways Plc (BA) shares ascended to a record high on Wednesday, with dealers saying a "split" order -- where a client deals through different brokers -- had met a shortage of stock and squeezed the price higher.
"There was a split order and that just exaggerated the move," said one senior sales trader.
Dealers cited a number of possible factors for the interest in BA, including an upbeat first-half results statement from Airtours Plc, up 30p at 974-1/2.
There were also indications from American Airlines that it expects word soon from the new British government on its stance towards the planned alliance between the two airlines.
BA shares were up 25-1/2p at 737 by 0954 GMT in volume of 1.7 million shares, surpassing its previous peak of 715p set on May 13 and leaving the stock up 22 percent since the end of last year.

Airtours said winter pre-tax losses narrowed by 45 percent to 12.67 million stg, about two million less than the market expected, and that booking levels and load factors for this summer were "showing appreciable gains."

Separately, American president Donald Carty said on Tuesday the airline expected to receive word from the new British government within the next couple of weeks as to whether it would consider the proposed alliance of the two carriers.

Carty said the position of the newly-elected British government toward the proposed alliance was still not clear, though the alliance could not afford to give up a large amount of its slots at London's Heathrow Airport in order to soften competition concerns and to quicken the pace of the approval.
